sections.title: The letter er
paragraphs: The letter (эр) /ɛr/ makes two sounds. Its main sound is a rolled sound. You hear it in (рука) /rʊˈka/, which means hand or arm. This consonant can be hard or soft. Consonant means a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. The letter makes two sounds in total.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air over the tip so it vibrates quickly. Your voice stays on. For the second sound, lift the middle of your tongue toward the roof of the mouth. Keep the tip vibrating against the gum ridge. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration of your vocal cords.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter has two sounds. Before hard vowels and plain consonants, say the hard rolled sound as in (рыба) /ˈrɨbə/ and (брат) /brat/. At the end of a word, it stays hard. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, make the sound palatalized. Palatalized means a consonant said with the middle of the tongue raised toward the roof of the mouth. You hear this softer sound in (река) /rʲɪˈka/ and (дверь) /dvʲerʲ/.

sections.title: Tips for English
paragraphs: Do not make the smooth sound of red or car. In that sound, your tongue curls back and never touches the roof of your mouth. For this letter, you must tap the tip of your tongue against your upper gum. It is like the quick sound in water when you say it fast. Relax your tongue tip so the air can roll it.
